segments.text: These lenses have the same focal length. Yet their rays do not land in the same tiny spot.
segments.say: These lenses have the same focal length. Yet their rays do not land in the same tiny spot.

segments.text: One looks better at the centre of the image, but that is only one place to look.
segments.say: One looks better at the centre of the image, but that is only one place to look.

segments.text: Which lens should we build? First, we have to decide what better means.
segments.say: Which lens should we build? First, we have to decide what better means.

segments.text: Lens design begins with a measurable task, not a favourite shape.
segments.say: Lens design begins with a measurable task, not a favourite shape.

segments.text: Recall the ray tracer: intersect a surface, find its normal, then apply Snell's law at each boundary.
segments.say: Recall the ray tracer: intersect a surface, find its normal, then apply Snell's law at each boundary.

segments.text: Send a bundle from one distant object point through the entrance aperture. Each ray reaches a different position on the detector.
segments.say: Send a bundle from one distant object point through the entrance aperture. Each ray reaches a different position on the detector.

segments.text: Their mean position is the spot's centroid. Measure each ray's distance from that centre.
segments.say: Their mean position is the spot's centroid. Measure each ray's distance from that centre.

segments.text: Square those distances, average them, and take the square root. That gives the RMS geometric spot radius.
segments.say: Square those distances, average them, and take the square root. That gives the root mean square geometric spot radius.

segments.text: Smaller means a tighter ray bundle, for this aperture and detector plane. It does not yet describe diffraction.
segments.say: Smaller means a tighter ray bundle, for this aperture and detector plane. It does not yet describe diffraction.

segments.text: We score spread around each centroid, so image position and distortion remain separate requirements.
segments.say: We score spread around each centroid, so image position and distortion remain separate requirements.

segments.text: Now choose the design variables. Our lens has two spherical surfaces, with curvatures given by inverse radius.
segments.say: Now choose the design variables. Our lens has two spherical surfaces, with curvatures given by inverse radius.

segments.text: Keep the glass index, centre thickness, entrance aperture, and wavelength fixed. The effective focal length stays fifty millimetres.
segments.say: Keep the glass index, centre thickness, entrance aperture, and wavelength fixed. The effective focal length stays fifty millimetres.

segments.text: Change the bending parameter, q. It redistributes curvature between the two faces while we preserve the thick lens's paraxial power.
segments.say: Change the bending parameter, cue. It redistributes curvature between the two faces while we preserve the thick lens's paraxial power.

segments.text: Watch the lens change shape. Its rays meet the surfaces at different angles, so their aberrations change.
segments.say: Watch the lens change shape. Its rays meet the surfaces at different angles, so their aberrations change.

segments.text: Equal effective focal lengths do not guarantee equal back focal distances. The detector position is another design variable, shared by every field.
segments.say: Equal effective focal lengths do not guarantee equal back focal distances. The detector position is another design variable, shared by every field.

segments.text: For each bending, choose one detector plane for the chosen score. Never refocus each field separately.
segments.say: For each bending, choose one detector plane for the chosen score. Never refocus each field separately.

segments.text: Begin with an object point on the optical axis. Sweep the bending and find each shape's best on-axis detector plane.
segments.say: Begin with an object point on the optical axis. Sweep the bending and find each shape's best on-axis detector plane.

segments.text: Each dot on this curve comes from an actual traced bundle. Its height is the geometric spot radius.
segments.say: Each dot on this curve comes from an actual traced bundle. Its height is the geometric spot radius.

segments.text: The lowest part identifies a promising shape. Refine the search around it instead of choosing by appearance.
segments.say: The lowest part identifies a promising shape. Refine the search around it instead of choosing by appearance.

segments.text: This shape and detector plane reduce the on-axis spread, for the rays we have sampled.
segments.say: This shape and detector plane reduce the on-axis spread, for the rays we have sampled.

segments.text: But a good central spot is not a complete image. What happened away from the axis?
segments.say: But a good central spot is not a complete image. What happened away from the axis?

segments.text: Tilt the incoming bundles to three and six degrees. First, keep the on-axis design's lens, aperture, and detector unchanged.
segments.say: Tilt the incoming bundles to three and six degrees. First, keep the on-axis design's lens, aperture, and detector unchanged.

segments.text: Now each object direction produces its own spot. Off-axis bundles can become asymmetric and need not prefer the same bending.
segments.say: Now each object direction produces its own spot. Off-axis bundles can become asymmetric and need not prefer the same bending.

segments.text: Use a combined merit: the mean squared spot radius over the three sampled fields, with equal weights.
segments.say: Use a combined merit: the mean squared spot radius over the three sampled fields, with equal weights.

segments.text: Now optimize bending and one common detector plane for all three fields. Compare every resulting spot using the same scale.
segments.say: Now optimize bending and one common detector plane for all three fields. Compare every resulting spot using the same scale.

segments.text: The preferred lens depends on the task. Different field weights, a curved detector, or another aperture can change the answer.
segments.say: The preferred lens depends on the task. Different field weights, a curved detector, or another aperture can change the answer.

segments.text: An optimizer follows the score we write. It does not know which images we forgot to test.
segments.say: An optimizer follows the score we write. It does not know which images we forgot to test.

segments.text: A score also needs constraints. Reject shapes whose two surfaces collide within the required clear opening.
segments.say: A score also needs constraints. Reject shapes whose two surfaces collide within the required clear opening.

segments.text: Require every sampled entrance ray to reach the detector. A missed surface or failed transmission must not simply disappear from the average.
segments.say: Require every sampled entrance ray to reach the detector. A missed surface or failed transmission must not simply disappear from the average.

segments.text: Otherwise, throwing away the difficult rays could make a bad lens look excellent.
segments.say: Otherwise, throwing away the difficult rays could make a bad lens look excellent.

segments.text: Likewise, shrinking the aperture would change the light collection and the task. We hold it fixed throughout this comparison.
segments.say: Likewise, shrinking the aperture would change the light collection and the task. We hold it fixed throughout this comparison.

segments.text: Search only the feasible designs, and keep the rejected cases visible. The boundary of the search is part of the result.
segments.say: Search only the feasible designs, and keep the rejected cases visible. The boundary of the search is part of the result.

segments.text: Before trusting the selected lens, trace a denser pupil sample. Then test directions between the fields used in the score.
segments.say: Before trusting the selected lens, trace a denser pupil sample. Then test directions between the fields used in the score.

segments.text: Check that the reported improvement survives. This tests sampling and generalization within our stated ray model.
segments.say: Check that the reported improvement survives. This tests sampling and generalization within our stated ray model.

segments.text: It does not validate everything outside that model. Here the glass index is constant, so chromatic aberration is absent by assumption.
segments.say: It does not validate everything outside that model. Here the glass index is constant, so chromatic aberration is absent by assumption.

segments.text: Nor is a cloud of ray intersections a diffraction point-spread function. Even a perfect geometric focus has a finite wave-optical spot.
segments.say: Nor is a cloud of ray intersections a diffraction point spread function. Even a perfect geometric focus has a finite wave optical spot.

segments.text: Episode three supplies that diffraction scale. Episode ten explains how a chosen objective can guide many design variables with gradients.
segments.say: Episode three supplies that diffraction scale. Episode ten explains how a chosen objective can guide many design variables with gradients.

segments.text: This example searches one bending parameter and solves for a shared detector position. It is not a Maxwell adjoint optimization or a universal best lens.
segments.say: This example searches one bending parameter and solves for a shared detector position. It is not a Maxwell adjoint optimization or a universal best lens.

segments.text: Lens design is a loop: specify a task, trace the rays, measure performance, then change the prescription under constraints.
segments.say: Lens design is a loop: specify a task, trace the rays, measure performance, then change the prescription under constraints.

segments.text: Keep the whole comparison honest: the same aperture, one shared detector plane, all tested fields, and no silently discarded rays.
segments.say: Keep the whole comparison honest: the same aperture, one shared detector plane, all tested fields, and no silently discarded rays.

segments.text: The next questions are practical. What changes across colour, and what can several elements correct that one singlet cannot?
segments.say: The next questions are practical. What changes across colour, and what can several elements correct that one singlet cannot?

segments.text: Start by asking what better means. Then build a model that can honestly answer.
